A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same LaDiR research work and complete, readable material across 29 pages. Pages 3–29, including Appendices A–E, have identical extracted text and rendered content; changes are confined to pages 1–2.

before.justification: v5 reports original mathematical reasoning, code-generation, and Countdown experiments in Tables 1–3, alongside ablations and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The VAE architecture, blockwise latent diffusion, two-stage training, answer generation, and diversity guidance remain identical in Section 3 and Appendix E.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate seven mathematics benchmarks, MBPP/MBPP+/HumanEval/HumanEval+, and Countdown CD-4/CD-5. Code generation is newly named in the abstract but was already evaluated in v5 Section 4.2; training datasets are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3 and the appendix comparisons. The added introduction sentence refers to the same AR SFT baseline already evaluated in Table 2.

E3.justification: Reported splits, sample sizes, metrics, model backbones, training budgets, and testing procedures remain identical in Section 4 and Appendix D. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Sections 4.4–4.5 and Appendices B–C retain the same ablations of noise, guidance, objectives, block size, augmentation, and blockization, together with the same compute, latency, and reasoning case analyses.

E5.justification: Repeated-run and seed information, statistical estimation descriptions, and uncertainty reporting are unchanged, including all table and figure reporting practices.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are retained. The introduction's added 5.2% improvement statement repeats v5 Section 4.2: Table 2 reports identical average Pass@1 values of 74.5% for LaDiR and 69.3% for AR SFT, a 5.2-percentage-point difference.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, training losses, flow-matching formulation, diversity-guidance equations, and diffusion derivations in Sections 2–3 and Appendix B remain identical.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction now highlight code generation and its existing performance advantage. Section 4.2 already reported this advantage, and v5's conclusion already included code generation; the scientific scope and core contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning semantic refinement, diversity, planning, interpretability, and accuracy–compute trade-offs remain unchanged. The added introduction sentence summarizes an existing result without adding a mechanism explanation or applicability qualification.

D1.justification: Section 9, Appendices D–E, and Table 13 retain the same implementation details, hyperparameters, processing descriptions, and supplementary code-release statement. No reproducibility information or resource access instructions are added.

R1.justification: Section 5, Appendix A, and the bibliography are unchanged. Austin et al. (2021) and Chen (2021), repeated in the new introduction sentence, were already cited for the coding benchmarks in v5.

P1.justification: The abstract now explicitly lists code generation and specifies puzzle planning. The introduction adds a short summary of existing coding results with benchmark citations, and the version/date stamp changes; the document structure is retained.

P2.justification: The abstract has different line wrapping, and page 2 has small spacing and positioning adjustments around Figure 1 and the expanded introduction. Figure content, captions, table designs, and all subsequent pages remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v6 gives a more complete overview by aligning the abstract and introduction with the code-generation evaluation already present in Section 4.2, Table 2, and the conclusion. This modestly improves clarity and consistency; the methods, empirical support, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
